chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Husayn, from Amr ibn Uthman, from Hanan ibn Sadeer, from Abdullah ibn Dinar, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:

He said: 'O Abdullah! There is no Eid for the Muslims, neither Al-Adha nor Al-Fitr, except that it renews grief for the Progeny of Muhammad (peace be upon them) within it.' I said, 'And why is that?' He said, 'Because they see their rights in the hands of others.'

key_terms.فِطْرٍ: Eid al-Fitr (Festival of Breaking the Fast)

ai.seo_question: Why do the festivals of Eid renew the grief of the Ahl al-Bayt?
ai.summary: In this hadith from al-Kafi, Imam al-Baqir (AS) highlights the poignant contrast between the joy of Eid and the enduring sorrow of the Ahl al-Bayt, who mourn the political and spiritual marginalization of their rightful Imamate. This narrative underscores the Shia theological concept of 'Ghurbah' (alienation), where the Prophet's family remains distinct from the prevailing caliphate, turning festive occasions into reminders of their suppressed authority. The Imam’s explanation links communal celebration directly to the historical reality of the Ahl al-Bayt's exclusion from leadership, framing their grief as a conscious recognition of divine right versus human usurpation.

en.hubeali:
Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ali Bin Al Husayn, from Amro Bin Usman, from Hanan Bin Sadeyr, from Abdullah Bin Dinar, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘O Abdullah! There is none from an Eid of the Muslims, be it Al-Azha, or Fitr, except that it renews grief to the Progeny<sup>asws</sup> of Muhammad<sup>saww</sup> in it’. I said, ‘And why is that so?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Because they<sup>asws</sup> are seeing their<sup>asws</sup> rights in the hands of others’.
en.sarwar: 2. Ahmad ibn Muhammad has narrated from Ali ibn al-Husayn from ‘Amr ibn ‘Uthman from Hanan ibn Sadir from ‘Abd Allah ibn Dinar who has said the following: “Abu Ja’far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘O ‘Abd Allah, every ‘Id, like al-Adha’ or al-Fitr that comes renews the sadness for Ale (family of) Muhammad, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause?’
I then asked, ‘Why is it so?’ He (the Imam) replied, ‘Because they see their rights in the hands of others?”
